findings.where: 'Good for' section: all twelve tag pills (First-time surfers, Remote workers, Long stays, Meeting people, Yoga, Nightlife, Budget, Cafés, Couples, Solo travellers, Scooter riders, Sunsets), on desktop and phone
findings.fault: Each tag is a filled, edged pill in a strong colour with short label text, so it looks like a filter chip or a button. None of them does anything (parts.txt p6–p17). Five also use a link's colour. On a site that will be about filtering hostels, they read as 'tap to see hostels good for surfers' or as a filter that can be switched on. Tapping does nothing and shows nothing.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker on a phone, deciding whether Canggu suits them. They will tap 'Meeting people' or 'Budget' expecting matching hostels or more detail, get no response, and think the page is broken or still loading on a poor connection.

findings.where: The 'coming soon' announcement block after 'What to look for', on desktop and phone
findings.fault: The notice that listings are not live yet sits in a solid dark red box. Red is the site's colour for errors and sold-out states. A plain 'not live yet' message is dressed as a failure or an alert, so the warning colour stands for two different things on the site.
findings.who_objects: A visitor reaching the end of the guide reads a red box as 'something went wrong' or 'Canggu is unavailable'. That is the wrong impression just as the page is telling them the product is coming. The founder would object too, because their rules keep the danger colour for errors and sold-out states.

findings.where: Nav and footer links: 'How we rank' (nav p4 and footer p23), 'Privacy', 'Terms', 'Report content' (footer), the wordmark 'MantaHostels home' (p1), and nav 'Destinations' (p3 → #destinations)
findings.fault: These links look like links but lead nowhere. 'How we rank', 'Privacy', 'Terms', 'Report content' and the home wordmark all point back to this same page. 'Destinations' jumps to a '#destinations' section that this page does not show. Every navigation route except the email link is dead.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who wants to know how hostels will be ranked, or who wants to look at another destination, clicks and stays where they are. The trust page that the site's merit-ranking claim depends on cannot be reached, and the page leaves them nowhere to go next.

findings.where: The 'Vibe' section heading, on desktop and phone
findings.fault: 'Vibe' is set in italic turquoise and underlined, which is the site's link look. It is a static heading (p5). Its sibling heading 'Surf' is plain, so one heading looks like a link and the other does not.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning the guide taps 'Vibe' expecting more about Canggu's crowd or nightlife, and nothing happens. It is a small trap, but it teaches them that underlined text on this site is not always a link.

findings.where: The end of the guide body, after the 'coming soon' notice
findings.fault: The page has no action at all. Once a visitor has judged that Canggu suits them, they get no next step: no way to be told when listings go live, and no working route to another destination or to how ranking works. The guide ends in a dead end.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker planning their next hop, who has just been told listings are 'coming soon' and has no way to act on it. They leave and do not come back. The founder loses the one visitor this pre-launch page could have kept.
